NO. 055 · Coast & Tidal Flats / Recurvirostridae · Stilts & Avocets

Pied Avocet

反嘴鹬 · fǎn zuǐ yù Recurvirostra avosetta
Winter visitor Uncommon 42–46 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

An upturned bill that sweeps the water from side to side

Black and white, with fine long legs, and most curious of all a bill that curves upward — like a pair of forceps that has been bent. It feeds by laying the tip of that bill on the surface and sweeping it from side to side as it walks; the action is quite unlike anything else.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • BillFine, long and conspicuously upturned, black — the most iconic feature of the species.
  • PlumageWhite throughout, with black from the crown to the nape and on the shoulders and wing coverts, making bold blocks of black and white.
  • LegsFine and long, blue-grey, about half the bird's height.
  • SizeSlender, fairly long-necked and very upright — elegant in the manner of a stilt.

Behaviour

Its feeding method is remarkable: the upturned bill tip is dipped into shallow water and swept from side to side, small crustaceans and insect larvae found by touch and snapped up — the upturn evolved precisely for this sweeping technique. Usually in flocks, and it mixes with other waders. A winter visitor in South China, in smaller numbers than Black-winged Stilt.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Jinwan salt pans
  • Qi'ao Island tidal flats
  • Hengqin wetlands
  • Doumen shallow ponds
Field note
You need look at nothing but the bill: upturned means Pied Avocet, dead straight means another wader.
